cues: A memoir is not an autobiography.
An autobiography covers a life; a memoir takes one remembered episode and tells it so the reader understands why it is still remembered.
A single, narrow slice of time: a morning, one journey.
Sensory detail: what could be seen, heard, smelt and touched, which is where the content marks are.
The double voice: the person it happened to, and the older person telling it.
And a turning point, with a reflection.
